issues.description: The template's Stock class declares findStockIngredient with two parameters (String name, boolean caseSensitive) but other methods in the same template (add, take) call findStockIngredient with a single String parameter. The problem statement UML and the solution implementation both define findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient. This mismatch causes a compilation error in the template and conflicts with the specified API students are expected to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock.findStockIngredient signature to match the specification and solution: declare public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (single parameter). Alternatively, add an overloaded one-parameter method that delegates to the two-parameter version. Ensure all internal calls (add, take, etc.) use the single-parameter signature so the template compiles and matches the problem API.

issues.description: The problem statement and reference solution expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single String parameter) but the template repository provides Stock.findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (an extra caseSensitive boolean parameter). This mismatch in the method signature forces students to reconcile two different APIs for the same concept (finding a stock ingredient by name) and may cause confusion or compilation issues when following the instructions or using the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the problem statement and solution by adding or exposing a single-parameter method Stock.findStockIngredient(String). Either change the template method signature to findStockIngredient(String) or add an overloaded wrapper method public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the existing two-parameter implementation (e.g., defaulting caseSensitive as appropriate). This ensures students can directly follow the problem description and match the reference solution.
